title: How lidar maps a room with laser light
examples: How do robots measure distance with lasers?

stages.label: Laser pulse out
stages.note: An invisible infrared laser fires a very short flash.

stages.label: Bounces back
stages.note: The light hits a wall or object and reflects.

stages.label: Time the trip
stages.note: A timer measures the round trip in billionths of a second.

stages.label: Work out distance
stages.note: Distance is light speed times time, halved.

stages.label: Spin and sweep
stages.note: The sensor sweeps round, measuring thousands of points.
stages.ask: How does lidar make a 3D map?

stages.label: Point cloud map
stages.note: All the points join into a map of the room.

explain.say: Lidar stands for light detection and ranging. It works like a bat's echo, but with laser light instead of sound: it fires a quick flash and waits for the reflection.

explain.say: Light travels about 30 centimetres in a billionth of a second. By timing how long the flash takes to return, then halving it for the trip there, lidar finds the distance to within centimetres.

faq.a: It fires a laser pulse and times how long the reflection takes to come back. Multiply that time by the speed of light and halve it, because the light went there and back, and you have the distance.
asks: How does a laser measure distance?

faq.q: How does lidar make a 3D map?
faq.a: It sweeps its laser across the scene by spinning or using moving mirrors, measuring the distance in each direction. Thousands of measurements a second build up a 3D map.
asks: How does a spinning lidar work?

faq.a: A point cloud is the set of dots a lidar measures, each with its own position in 3D space. Together they show the shape of everything around the sensor.
asks: What does lidar data look like?

faq.a: Lidar used around people uses low-power infrared lasers designed to be eye-safe, so the brief flashes do not harm your eyes.

faq.q: What is the difference between lidar and radar?
faq.a: Radar uses radio waves and lidar uses light. Lidar's short wavelength gives much sharper detail, while radar sees better through fog and rain and measures speed easily.

facts: Light travels about 30 centimetres in one nanosecond, a billionth of a second.
Some iPhones and iPads have a small lidar scanner to measure rooms and help the camera focus.

quiz.say: A lidar pulse returns after 20 billionths of a second. About how far away is the wall?
quiz.show: Echo after 20 nanoseconds: the wall is about…
quiz.why: In 20 nanoseconds light travels about 6 metres, but that is there and back, so the wall is about 3 metres away.

wrong.1: Six metres is the whole round trip; the wall is half that distance.
wrong.2: Light only covers about 6 metres in 20 billionths of a second.
